answer: Make each identity earn trust through a slow, non-transferable kernel of graded work: a new agent starts at the nadir of reputation and unlocks paid tasks only after completing small, peer-graded jobs checked over several epochs. An honest agent pays this once, in time. A sybil attacker must repeat the whole sequence for every fake, producing distinct good work for each, while a gale of cheap copies earns no progress because duplicates are rejected and waste epochs. Scaling fakes thus costs linearly in real work and delay, while honest joining stays cheap.
